summary: JINOTEXAS developed Sistema Landsat, a bilingual web viewer that helps students and researchers investigate environmental change using a flat map, an interactive 3D globe, and historical charts. The viewer combines 40 Environmental Performance Index indicators for 220 territories from 1995 to 2022 with three NASA data subsets for Sébaco, Nicaragua. To demonstrate traceability, users can reproduce Nicaragua’s unsafe sanitation score, which rose from 13.84 to 43.86 points, directly from the original EPI data. They can also explore annual temperatures from NASA POWER, a MODIS vegetation summary, and an eight-day dry spell from MERRA‑2. Each result shows its source, units, and coverage so users can explain what changed and understand the limits of the evidence.
details:
What the project does. Sistema Landsat turns environmental data exploration into a guided investigation. In Cases, secondary-school students follow clues and get feedback. In Explore, users select an indicator, territory, and time window, then compare two periods and inspect the underlying values. In Analyze, users can play through the years on the globe, estimate the magnitude of change, and export the series with its source and units. Where suitable data are available, seven candidate models are evaluated for forecasts one to three years ahead against a last-value baseline.

How we prepared and verified the data. We rebuilt the viewer’s EPI dataset from 40 original CSV files, preserving decimal values, valid zeros, and missing-data reasons. The published dataset contains 246,400 indicator–territory–year records, including 212,576 numeric scores and 33,824 missing records with documented reasons. In the viewer, Nicaragua’s unsafe sanitation score rises from 13.84 to 43.86 EPI points between 1995 and 2022, with a descriptive Theil–Sen slope of approximately +1.20 points per year. The EPI series may include interpolation and constant extensions, so we report this as a descriptive result.

How we used NASA data. For Sébaco, we integrated 11 annual averages of two-meter air temperature from NASA POWER for 2015–2025, calculated from 4,018 daily records. We also integrated a mean NDVI of 0.576 from 21 accepted MODIS composites in 2025 and a longest dry spell of eight consecutive days from the selected MERRA‑2 grid cell in January 2026. The viewer identifies the NDVI and dry-spell values as summaries of their respective periods.

Tools and intended impact. We built the viewer using React, TypeScript, and Vite. We used Python for data preparation and SQL Server during the initial transformation. The local production build and 19 automated tests passed. The pixel-art globe gives students a way into the investigation, while the source information and export tools let advanced users check and reproduce results.
